question.text: For a good quality cement, the ratio of silica to alumina is found to be

solution.text: For a good quality cement the ratio of silica (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>SiO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>) and alumina (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Al</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math>) should be between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>to</mi><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn></math>. Similarly, the ratio of lime (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>CaO</mi></math>) to the total oxide mixtures consisting of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>SiO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>Al</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Fe</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> should be roughly <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, If lime is in excess, the cement cracks during setting.
